columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Available on web, iOS, and Android.
Built around the belief that best recommendations come from people you know and trust, not purely engagement-optimized algorithms.
Personal library with custom shelves; follow readers; share highlights and notes (export to X, Instagram, WhatsApp, etc.).
Book clubs with schedules, discussion threads, shared progress; moderators approve members, manage books, and set permissions.

strengths.title: Social-first design for readers
strengths.detail: Clean, minimal interface focused on social reading, follow people over algorithms; not cluttered by ads or excessive features.

strengths.title: Integrated book clubs, not bolted-on groups
strengths.detail: Clubs are core: schedules, discussions, shared progress, and highlight-based conversations.

strengths.title: Highlight-centric sharing
strengths.detail: Encourages sharing impactful passages across social channels, strengthening conversation around books.

strengths.title: Good fit for modern book communities
strengths.detail: Works well with online fandoms and BookTok-style communities that want to track, share, and discuss beyond generic feeds.

weaknesses.title: Smaller catalog and user base vs incumbents
weaknesses.detail: Still growing; may lack depth of ratings/reviews for obscure titles that Goodreads or LibraryThing have.

weaknesses.title: Freemium details evolving
weaknesses.detail: Premium features and pricing are changing; some readers may be unclear about long-term cost vs free tier.

weaknesses.title: Less advanced analytics than StoryGraph
weaknesses.detail: Strong on social reading and clubs; weaker on mood/pace analytics and deep reading stats.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Literal (Literal Club) is minimalist social reading app, personal library, highlights/notes, follow trusted readers, and real book clubs with schedules and discussion. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Literal is a minimalist social reading app where you build a personal library, share highlights and notes, follow trusted readers, and join real book clubs to discuss books together. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Literal (Literal Club) side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Literal (Literal Club) you can use Ebook and Community & Messaging as first-class product jobs. You need a dedicated reader, a giant store, or social tracking of everything you have ever read.

Using Kahana with Literal (Literal Club)

You can use both. Literal (Literal Club) keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the reader or tracker you already use. Put the Club pick, discussion questions, and related files on Kahana so the book is a shared library item, not only a private progress bar.
